title: [finding] service-automation's parallel-branches test grades a real wall-clock window with a 100 ms bound five times the sequential path it claims to rule out — it cannot fail on its regression and can fail on a slow runner
body:
① — a test that cannot detect the regression it names, and can fail on runner speed alone.

Filed by the `domain:spec` execution seat 1 (seat post #6017, `session_013RDBh5DqXd2xnLwvHLgLFr`), 2026-09-23. ⛔ Unlabelled beyond `finding`, ⛔ ungraded, ⛔ unrouted. Suggested lane: `domain:services` (`packages/services/*`). ⛔ This seat does not fix it: it is outside this lane, and the lane rule is 「谁发现 flake 谁修或立单,⛔ 不绕行」 — this is the filing half.

## The assertion, read at source

`origin/main` `dc1b98680b`, `packages/services/service-automation/src/engine.test.ts`, the end of the parallel-branches case:

```ts
const start = Date.now();
const result = await engine.execute('parallel_flow');
const elapsed = Date.now() - start;
// Parallel execution should be faster than sequential (10+10=20ms)
// Allow generous margin but expect it's faster than fully sequential
expect(elapsed).toBeLessThan(100); // generous but parallel should be ~15ms
```

The two branches carry `config: { delay: 10 }`.

## Why it is two defects in one line

1. **It cannot fail on the regression it documents.** By its own comment the fully **sequential** path is `10 + 10 = 20 ms`, and 20 < 100. A regression that serialised the branches would still pass. The bound is five times the time it claims to rule out, so it does not separate parallel from sequential at any runner speed.
2. **It can fail on runner speed alone.** The assertion grades a real `Date.now()` window, so on a slow or contended runner a correct parallel engine exceeds 100 ms and goes red. ⇒ a phantom check that is also a flake source.

## ⚠️ How it surfaced — a candidate, ⛔ not a proven cause

`Test Core (3/6)` went red on PR #19752 at head `c06eec4029` (run 35799036431, job 106984977747). The check run's own annotation names the package: `command (…/packages/services/service-automation) pnpm run test exited (1)`. The round that diagnosed it ruled out both of the other candidates, measured rather than argued:

- the package's suite at that head, closure built: **141 files / 1690 tests, exit 0**;
- the **exact** tree CI tested (`git merge-tree --write-tree c06eec4029 2bdb81f8ad` ⇒ `677a82c694…`, materialised and re-hashed identical): **exit 0**;
- the base move could not reach the package (one commit, `packages/spec/src/ui/component.zod.ts`; the four `dist` bundles byte-identical built both ways; the package imports `@objectstack/spec/ui` zero times); the PR's changeset line could not either (package-local tests only).

And two later heads of the same PR ran that shard **green**. ⇒ a non-deterministic failure on that runner.

⛔ **The failing assertion was never read**: the job log's redirect target is refused at this container's egress gateway (`productionresultssa6.blob.core.windows.net:443`, gateway 403 to CONNECT). So this card does ⛔ not claim this assertion caused that red. It stands on its own reading above — both defects are visible in the source whether or not it was the one that fired.

## ⛔ What is NOT claimed

- ⛔ No repair chosen. A shape assertion (branch start stamps overlapping, or an instrumented clock) and a bound that actually sits between the parallel and sequential times are both coherent; which is right depends on what the `script` node's `delay` really does, which this seat did not measure.
- ⛔ No census of other wall-clock assertions in this package or elsewhere.

## Dedupe

Repo-scoped issue search, query 「service-automation engine.test parallel branches elapsed toBeLessThan wall-clock flaky timing assertion」: 25 results including closed — ⚠️ relevance-ranked, so ⛔ not a count of matching cards. None names this assertion. Nearest in shape: #19631 (open; a different test, `dev-plugin-tenancy-posture.test.ts`, timing out at 5000 ms) and #17079 (closed duplicate; `turso-driver-timeout.test.ts` racing its own 100 ms window).
